title: Freedom from slavery and forced labour
summary: No one may hold you in slavery or servitude, and you cannot be forced to perform forced or compulsory labour.
body_plain: As part of your right to dignity, the Constitution says no person shall be held in slavery or servitude, and no person shall be required to perform forced or compulsory labour. There are narrow, defined exceptions (such as work done as part of a lawful court sentence, or normal communal obligations), but you cannot simply be compelled to labour for someone against your will.
rights: You may not be held in slavery or servitude (s.34(1)(b)).
You may not be forced to perform forced or compulsory labour (s.34(1)(c)).
Only narrow, lawful exceptions apply (e.g. a lawful court sentence).
do_list: Refuse forced labour calmly and ask on what lawful basis it is demanded.
Record who is compelling you and how.
Report the matter to the NHRC or a lawyer.
dont_list: Do not accept that anyone can force you to work against your will.
Do not sign away this right under pressure.
common_situations: Someone uses threats, withheld documents, debt, confinement, or violence to force you to work.
You cannot leave a workplace or household safely and your pay or identity documents are controlled.
A child or vulnerable person is compelled to work in dangerous or exploitative conditions.
words_to_use: I am not working voluntarily and I need help to leave safely.
My identity documents or wages are being withheld.
Please contact an appropriate protection agency or trusted person without alerting the person controlling me.
if_violated: Prioritise a safe exit plan; do not confront a controller alone if doing so could increase danger.
When safe, preserve identity details, locations, payment records, messages, travel documents, and witness contacts.
Contact emergency services, NAPTIP, a lawyer, or a trusted protection organisation for specialised help.
